wu: Travel Bingo: Students get a bingo grid with travel experiences (e.g., 'I have been to Paris', 'I have tried sushi'). They mingle, ask classmates 'Have you ever...?', and mark off squares. First to get a line shouts 'Bingo!'
wuAlt: Travel Charades: Teacher writes travel verbs on cards (e.g., 'pack a suitcase', 'miss a flight'). Students act them out for classmates to guess using 'Have you ever...?'
Travel Pictionary: Students draw travel-related words (e.g., 'beach', 'passport') while others guess in full sentences.
pres: Teacher shows a photo of a crowded Eid celebration and asks 'Where have you been for Eid?'. Models 'I have been to my grandparents' house' and 'I have gone to the souk'. Uses flashcards of travel destinations to drill 'been/gone'. Checks understanding with 'Ask me: Where have you been?'
presAlt: Travel Story: Teacher reads a short story about a holiday using present perfect and past simple (e.g., 'I have been to Spain. I saw the Sagrada Familia'). Students underline the target forms.
Travel Video: Plays a 1-minute vlog clip where the narrator uses 'been/gone'. Students note down all examples.
prac: Escape Room Puzzle: Groups receive a locked box with 4 grammar clues (e.g., 'Find a sentence with been to Egypt'). They solve travel-themed grammar questions to get the code. Teacher provides a 'been/gone' reference sheet for support.
pracAlt: Grammar Relay: Teams race to write correct 'been/gone' sentences on the board based on prompts (e.g., 'You are not here now' → 'He has gone to the market').
Travel Timeline: Students create a personal timeline of travel experiences using 'I have been to...' and 'I went to...'.
ls: Listening to Travel Dialogues: Students listen to two friends talking about Eid and a summer holiday. They complete a table comparing 'What they did' (past simple) and 'Where they have been' (present perfect). Checks comprehension of time expressions.
re: Travel Freeze: Teacher shouts a travel destination (e.g., 'London!'). Students freeze and say 'I have been to London!' or 'I have gone to London!'. If they hesitate, they sit down.
prod: Eid vs. Holiday Venn Diagram: In pairs, students compare Eid al-Fitr with a holiday abroad (e.g., Christmas) using a Venn diagram. They write 8 sentences comparing traditions, food, and activities. Then, they share their findings with the class.
rw: Travel Blog Writing: Students read a short travel blog entry (60 words) about a holiday. They identify examples of present perfect and past simple. Then, they write their own 60-word blog entry about a travel experience using both tenses.
st: Travel Song: Play 'I've Been Everywhere' by Johnny Cash (edited version). Students sing along and list places mentioned. End with: 'Today we practiced talking about travel experiences using present perfect. Thank you, class!'
g: Students match travel photos with present perfect sentences ('I have seen the pyramids').
Teams race to categorize sentences into 'been' or 'gone' columns.
Students survey classmates about travel experiences using 'Have you ever...?' and report back.
Students add one sentence to a story using present perfect or past simple.
Teams take turns drawing travel words for others to guess in sentences.
diff: Fast finishers: Write 5 more sentences comparing Eid with another holiday.
Support learners: Use sentence starters ('I have been to...', 'I have gone to...') for the Venn diagram.
hw: Write a KET-style email (25+ words) to a friend about your best Eid holiday.
Write 8 sentences comparing Eid with Christmas or another holiday.
Create a travel poster using 5 present perfect sentences about places you want to visit.
tip: Use the American Space Oujda context to connect travel themes—e.g., 'Have you been to the American Space for an event?'—to make language practice relevant and engaging for learners.
